bug_semantics: Netmaker exposed an HTTP handler that terminates the server process with syscall.Kill(Getpid(), SIGINT). As shipped this was POST /api/server/shutdown in controllers/server.go serverHandlers, registered with no Authorize, allowUsers, or logic.SecurityCheck wrapper while neighboring /api/server routes used those wrappers. HttpMiddlewares carried no authentication (only an optional Pro unlicensed-API gate), so any network client could POST the endpoint and interrupt the process. With a restart supervisor this produced cyclic denial of service at roughly 3-second intervals. CVE-2026-29771 / GHSA-rhr9-hgcm-x289 (CWE-404); CVSS 4.0 PR:N matches the unauthenticated registration. The first code-level patch wrapped the handler in logic.SecurityCheck(true).

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2026-29771 is a live analyzed record (not withdrawn/rejected), matching GHSA-rhr9-hgcm-x289. The sink is an unauthenticated mux handler that sends SIGINT to the Netmaker PID, enabling unauthenticated cyclic DoS. Neighboring server routes were already wrapped; the shutdown route was added without that wrap and with no router-wide auth middleware. BIC search used -S/-L plus PR reconstruction rather than scanning for AI commits. PR #2672 is a four-commit squash onto develop; protocol forbids treating the squash aggregate as BIC when members are reconstructable. The smallest first-write of the SIGINT-without-auth mechanism is member 57f19cdc; 68d387a5/59add9dd only polish the handler and b1ece5f7 only renames it to the advisory path POST /api/server/shutdown. Parent 27378b9c was checked directly and lacks the handler. The develop squash 944405f0 is the carrier into tags from v0.22.0 through v1.2.0. The vendor patch is wrapping the handler in SecurityCheck(true) in f5752fa6, merged as db2f005e (#3776). Git tag v1.2.0 predates that merge and still contains the unauthenticated handler; first tagged release with the wrap is v1.4.0. That is a version-label mismatch, not a false positive.
